context: #091 Piece A (dungeon interior movement capture) attempted to make the engine BFS traverse closed doors by memory-poking door state, so an expanded reachability/passability table could be captured. The plan's poke target (the +0x240 door-record wall-plane) was falsified live; follow-up spikes falsified the per-cell door fields too. Conclusion: the door-block routes through the SAME uncracked dynamic gate as general collision (#087), not any static maze-table field. Nate's directive: escalate to the #087 collision RE as a sub-project.
summary: The engine's FORWARD-STEP block at a closed door is NOT enforced by any static maze-table field that a memory poke can flip. Live-verified at door cell (124,121,f2), region 0, cell-index ci=44 (z*64 + x*8 + y): three distinct poke hypotheses all left the engine refusing to step (UP moved=false). This confirms #087's thesis that forward passability is decided by dynamic render-classify state (the BSS plane at ~0x4e08 read by maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls 0x309d), recomputed per frame, and is invisible to static-field poking.
method: tools/libretro/trace-maze.ts `stepprobe 124,121,2` (drive to the door cell via movement.ts pathTo, read live fields, poke, tap UP, report whether the engine's party coords changed). Each hypothesis was a temporary instrumentation of phaseStepProbe (reverted after). Live dosbox-pure patched core (17 _dbp_ symbols, 2026-06-10 build).

findings.claim: The canonical level-0 entrance door is at gx124 gy121 facing 2 (north). When the party stands there facing 2: region 0, party cell x=5 y=4, cell-index ci = z*64 + x*8 + y = 44 (this x*8+y ordering is the correct one — the alternate z*64+y*8+x = 37 reads door-orientation 0, i.e. the wrong cell). The per-cell NORTH wall plane (recOff+0x60, 2-bit, recOff = *[0x4faa]) already reads 0 (OPEN) at this cell; the per-cell door-orientation (recOff+0x378, 2-bit) reads 2, which EQUALS the party facing (2) — the textbook 'closed door blocks when orientation==facing' condition from maze-door-open-mechanic.json. The per-cell special-index (recOff+0x1f8, 4-bit) reads 0.
findings.evidence: stepprobe 124,121,2 -> arrived(gx124,gy121,f2) region0 x5 y4 liveN=0 liveW=0; [diag] ci=44 sidx=0 dstate=2 | ciYX=37 sidx=0 dstate=0 | facing=2

findings.claim: Poking the door-record +0x240 wall-plane to OPEN (clear all four 2-bit facing fields; pointer *[0x4fa8], the table door-record.ts decodes and the table FORCE/PICK success edits via FUN_0000_88af) has ZERO effect on engine forward movement. A full collmap BFS with all 12 type-7 doors poked open reached 73 cells / 288 views — essentially the old entrance island (74/293); the cell north of the door (124,120) was still unreached.
findings.evidence: collmap (doors poked=12) -> 288 views / 73 cells, (124,120) reached=False, new reachable set is a SUBSET of the old. stepprobe with openAllDoors poke before the UP-tap: moved=false.

findings.claim: Replicating the engine's door_set (FUN_0000_6d62) OPEN writes on the per-cell table at *[0x4faa] does NOT unblock the step. Tested two variants at ci=44, both moved=false: (a) special-index +0x1f8 = 7 (engine-opened) + door-orientation +0x378 = 0; (b) special-index +0x1f8 = 0 (no door) + door-orientation +0x378 = 0. Variant (b) is the fully 'no door, open' state (sidx=0, dstate=0, north wall plane already 0) and the engine STILL refused to step north.
findings.evidence: [diag] after poke: ci sidx=7 -> moved=false (run 1); [diag] after poke (sidx=0,dstate=0): ci sidx=0 dstate=0 -> moved=false (run 2). liveN=0 throughout.

findings.claim: The forward-step block at this door is enforced by dynamic state the static maze-table fields do not cover — consistent with #087's finding that no static cell-feature combo predicts passability (best fit 28/120 errors) and that the real gate is maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls (0x309d) reading per-frame render-classify state. The specific next RE lead is the BSS plane the 0x309d tail reads: getbit_test(0x4e08-BSS, cell) at 0x3164/0x3173 (returns 1 -> block), plus getbit_test([bp+6], cell). That plane is written by the per-frame render-classify pass (#087: 'collision appears enforced via the per-frame render-classify (shared state)'). Cracking it needs core instrumentation (a READ-watchpoint on the 0x4e08 plane + backtrace, or single-step disasm of 0x309d 0x3148..0x3243), NOT field poking.
findings.evidence: Three independent static-field poke hypotheses falsified. Cross-ref docs/re/findings/maze-collision-model.json (CONCLUSION_2026-06-10, ROOT_OBSERVABILITY_WALL_2026-06-10, watchpoint_instrumentation_2026-06-10) and maze-door-open-mechanic.json (the 0x309d tail block-bit list).

implications: #091 Piece A (movement-first interior capture via door-poke) is NOT achievable by poking maze-table fields. The interior cannot be engine-captured past a closed door without either (1) cracking the 0x309d dynamic gate (the #087 sub-project) so doors can be opened in a way the engine's own movement honors, or (2) driving the engine through its real door-open path (FORCE/PICK success or a scripted special-square event) per door before capture — which only opens one door per success and is entangled with combat encounters. The deferred interior-render piece (Piece B) is unaffected by this (separate problem).
next_steps: Add a READ-watchpoint on the BSS plane at DGROUP ~0x4e08 (the dbp_rwatch_* instrumentation already exists in the patched core) during an OPEN forward step vs the BLOCKED door step; backtrace the writer to find the render-classify pass that sets the per-cell block bit.

Single-step / disasm maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls 0x309d tail 0x3148..0x3243 to pin exactly which getbit_test returns 1 for the blocked door cell (the door finding lists getbit_test([bp+6],cell) and getbit_test(0x4e08,cell) as the two block bits).
Confirm whether [bp+6] is a caller-passed dynamic mask (the render-classify output) vs a static table — that determines whether door-open is pokeable at all or strictly render-coupled.
